name: Employer falsely claims employee abandoned job
expected: Advises compiling leave approval emails, medical records, and responding refuting abandonment allegation.
prompt: I was on approved medical leave with doctor notes, but employer sent an email claiming I abandoned the job and owes them money.
raw_response:
I understand how stressful it is to receive such an alarming email while you are on medical leave.

### | Your Situation
You were on approved medical leave supported by doctor's notes when your employer sent an email accusing you of job abandonment and claiming that you owe them money. This creates an urgent employment dispute regarding wrongful termination, salary dues, and unwarranted financial claims.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 5 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, your employer is legally obligated to clear your earned wages on time, and withholding wages on fabricated grounds of job abandonment is unlawful.
- Under Section 7 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, any arbitrary or unauthorized financial deductions or demands made by an employer without a formal inquiry and legal basis are strictly prohibited.
- Under the applicable State Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, employers must follow proper statutory service conditions and cannot penalize employees who are absent due to genuine, certified medical reasons.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including copies of your approved medical leave applications, doctor's notes, medical certificates, and the email sent by your employer claiming job abandonment.
2. Send a written demand notice to your employer granting 15 days to retract the false job abandonment claim and release your unpaid earned wages.
3. Approach the appropriate forum, such as the local Labour Commissioner, by filing a formal complaint under Section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act for delayed or withheld wages.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. Did you receive written confirmation or approval from your employer or HR department before taking the medical leave?
2. What is the approximate amount of unpaid salary or money that your employer is claiming you owe them?

citations.act_name: State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts
citations.section: Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision
citations.title: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.
